findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how a batched pandoc invocation's combined output is re-split into per-unit wiki segments (e.g. insert a rare sentinel block between units in the batched input and split the output on the corresponding output marker), so original-order reassembly and per-unit fallback markers are achievable.

ABSENCE: the plan never states a demarcation mechanism (e.g. a sentinel block between units) to re-split one pandoc `-t jira` output stream into its N constituent unit outputs; pandoc jira output has no reliable unit delimiter
findings.finding: The batching approach does not specify how a single pandoc invocation's combined wiki output is split back into per-unit segments, which the plan needs for original-order reassembly (safe batches are interleaved with verbatim dangerous units per 271c) and for the promised per-unit fallback markers.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Restate that dangerous units are passed through verbatim WITHOUT any pandoc invocation (never 'rendered in their own invocation'), and clarify that the isolation intent is only that a dangerous unit is never batched with safe units so a batch fallback cannot degrade it.
evidence: Plan: 'a unit already flagged dangerous by 271c's classifier is rendered in its own single-unit invocation so its verbatim fallback cannot pull safe siblings down with it'
271c (show_ticket 271c-e88f-3220-4c9b) Approach: 'render structurally-safe units … via pinned pandoc; pass dangerous units (ASCII tables, arrow/regex/HTML-dense prose) through **verbatim**'
271c Context: 'pandoc's jira reader misparses -> , ASCII pipe-tables, and regex, and provably erodes them one character per pass' — the reason dangerous units are never sent to pandoc
findings.finding: The plan says a dangerous unit is 'rendered in its own single-unit invocation,' implying pandoc is run on it — but 271c passes dangerous units through VERBATIM without invoking pandoc at all, because pandoc's jira reader is what corrupts them.
findings.location: Approach → 'a unit already flagged dangerous by 271c's classifier is rendered in its own single-unit invocation'; AC line 2 ('a dangerous unit is rendered in its own single-unit invocation')
scenarios: An implementer reads 'dangerous unit rendered in its own single-unit invocation' literally and runs pandoc on an ASCII table / regex-dense body, reintroducing the exact per-pass erosion 271c's classifier exists to prevent.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'is rendered in its own single-unit invocation' with 'is emitted verbatim with no pandoc invocation and is never batched with safe units, so a batch-level fallback cannot degrade a safe sibling.'

findings.finding: The dependency-boundary premise mischaracterizes what prerequisite 271c delivers. The plan asserts 271c 'leaves WikiTextCodec fully identity and delivers wiki_render.py as a pure module not referenced by any codec op or live send path in that story (271c's own words)'. findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State a max batch size (or a fallback-blast-radius cap) so a single timeout/error degrades a bounded number of safe units to verbatim.

'degrade every unit in that invocation's batch to its original Markdown verbatim'
No maximum batch size or fallback-blast-radius cap stated
findings.finding: Batching is specified as 'as few pandoc invocations as correctness allows' with dangerous units rendered singly, but no upper bound on batch size is given — an unbounded batch means one late-arriving hang or non-zero exit degrades an arbitrarily large set of units to verbatim.
scenarios: A body of 500 safe units batched into one invocation times out; all 500 degrade to verbatim even though only one was pathological
findings.suggested_fix: Cap batch size at a stated N units per invocation so the verbatim-fallback blast radius on timeout is bounded and predictable.
